author: Winston Churchill
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Genuine love is not a transaction where you keep score of who gave what; it is a state of being where you extend warmth and goodwill without needing to control the other person.

In Winston Churchill's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. The biggest barrier to deep connection is never external; it is our own fear of rejection. We build armor around our hearts to avoid pain, but that same armor ends up locking out the warmth and intimacy we crave.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
